construct: a 7-column CSS grid of 35 auto-placed cells (5 weeks), the LAST carrying a distinct paint (rgb(160, 32, 160))
why: The month grid as a real library draws it: `grid-template-columns: repeat(7, ...)` with auto-placed day cells, which is what makes the 7-wide shape a STRUCTURAL fact rather than a consequence of wrapping. Separated from repeat-siblings-thirtyone on purpose - that case asks whether 31 siblings survive, this one asks whether they survive when the parent is a grid, where the committed frontier already shows every grid case refused on the canvas half.

canvas.note: a 7-column grid frame with 35 cell children

mustHave: the month grid is exactly 7 columns wide
there are exactly 35 cells, laid out as 5 rows of 7
the 35th (last) cell is a visibly different colour (magenta) from the other 34
columns line up vertically - cell N and cell N+7 share a left edge

predictedWall.why: conformance/README.md records the first canvas measurement verbatim: 'The 15 refusals are one wall: every grid case's captured contract has no definite root height, and the emitter refuses it by name (grid-axis-indefinite, FC-GRID-ROOT-VSIZE). The capture writes grid roots the canvas will not host.' A month grid is a grid root with an intrinsic height, so I expect it to land in exactly that bucket. FC-REPEAT-FORWARD-ABSENT (proposed above) applies on the capture half as well.
